- And my men?
442:
We'll return your charges
to prison today.
443:
If you find the coat attendant,
might you need us again?
444:
I didn't want to tell you,
but Bely—Docent—escaped today.
445:
It's incredible, but true.
It's dangerous for you to keep this disguise.
446:
Could it wait until tomorrow?
It is New Year, and they did try, in their own way.
447:
We're outside the city. It's unlikely
Docent could find us.
448:
All right, but don't set foot outside
the house. Oh, we forwarded your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev's wife.
Here's her reply, addressed to him.
450:
- You'll come to lunch on the first? Promise?
- We promise!
451:
What a shame. Such a nice woman,
and her father's a fence and profiteer.
452:
What's all this noise? Who said you could go out?
- He's back... The bad man.
454:
The New Year is here. I hope
everything changes for you this year.
455:
Anything may happen, but know this:
wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I'll always remember you.
I'll be sure to find you.
457:
- And now... Just a moment.
- Where's he off to?
458:
Who knows? You can't make sense
of him anymore.
459:
What's to make sense of? He said he'll
find us anywhere and slit our throats.
461:
They say he took a razor to Ryaby's throat.
One slice, goodbye.
- He's gone savage, that jackal.
462:
Who's here to call?
It's Father Frost, with presents for all!
463:
- Come here, Fedya. - What have I done?
- Come on. Wear these in good health. Slippers.
464:
- What do I need those for? I don't have a home.
- You will. There's still time.
465:
- Meanwhile, they'll come in handy in prison. Wear them.
- You always have to jinx things.
466:
This is for you, Vasya.
And this is for you, Gavrila Petrovich.
- Thank you.
467:
- Pure wool.
- This is for you too.
469:
Sour stuff.
It's dull without vodka.
470:
- Do you have to get drunk as a pig?
- What else is there to do?
471:
We could sit together
and have a heart-to-heart.
472:
I'm no prosecutor. I don't do heart-to-hearts.
- We could play a game.
473:
Listen to him! Think I'm a sucker
who'll play cards with you?

474: Why does it have to be cards?
475:
Here's a good game: cities.
I say "Moscow."
476:
You take the last letter, W,
and say "Warsaw." Then on W, "Winnipeg." See?
477: Now you, Fedya. A city beginning with G.
478:
Vorkuta.
Why? I did time there.
479:
- All right. You need one beginning with A.

480:

482:
- You'd do better to find our helmet.
- Be quiet.
483:
- We hide it while he peeks through a hole?
- Then you go out and hide it.
484:

485:
- I'll rip your mouth open, you little scoundrel!
- Always with the mouth...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- I was.
487:
- Did you have a mother and father?
- I did.
488:

490:
- He came on his own.
- Oh, you're here too.
491:
I was going to your place,
but I sensed an ambush.
492: Mitya, I need somewhere to hide.
494:
- Where are we going?
- Keep walking.
495:
- Sorry we called you out for nothing, Doctor.
- It's all right.
496:
Give him some valerian drops,
warm tea, and let him sleep.
- Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?

499:
"Dear Dad, we found out
you're in prison,
500:
and we were very happy,
because we thought you were dead."
501:
Who was the swine who told

502:
"Mom was happy too, because when
your letter came, she cried all day.
503:
Before that, she told us
you were a test pilot."
505:
"I'm glad you're alive anyway,
because Mom says
506:
you're a good man,

508:
Make tracks! I'll knock your horns off,

510:

511:

What's ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, nothing decent!
Come to your senses before it's too late.
513:

514:
- She won't. - Why not?

518:

520:

521:

523:

524:

527:
- What are you doing?
- Cleaning the carpet.
528:
Well, comrades, the show's over.

530:

531:

- Why a guard?
532:

533:

534:

535:

536:

537:
- Made me dive in that freezing weather!

541:

542:

- Let's go.

545:

- Two.
